dedupe_keys.name: toxic chemical sites at high or moderate risk of flooding new york times analysis excerpted by climate signals

description: This New York Times analysis overlaid the federal Toxics Release Inventory, which lists more than 21,600 facilities handling large amounts of toxic chemicals, with Federal Emergency Management Agency flood zones and found more than 2,500 such sites in flood-prone areas in every US state: over 1,400 in the highest-risk zones and about 1,100 in moderate-risk zones, with others just outside mapped zones. It cites past releases such as the Baytown, Texas, chemical plant flooded by Hurricane Harvey, a Florida fertiliser plant that leaked phosphoric acid and an Ohio refinery that released benzene, and links the risk to heavier rainfall, sea level rise and coastal storms. It was reported by Hiroko Tabuchi, Nadja Popovich, Blacki Migliozzi and Andrew Lehren for the New York Times, and the page read is an excerpt on the Climate Signals site, which links to the original maps. Coverage is national. The excerpt is free to read online, with no licence or date given. Caveats: it is journalism, the facility-level results were not seen, and flood zones understate risk as patterns shift. For simulation it shows how to combine chemical facility registers with flood maps for Natech hazard exposure screening. It is related to the EPA Toxics Release Inventory record in this catalogue, its main input.
